title: ExoGRU-guided experiments support RBM24 involvement in small-RNA secretion
summary: A recurrent model of RNA-sequence features helped nominate RNA-binding proteins involved in secretion. Perturbation and binding experiments supported RBM24 involvement in the tested cell system, alongside previously implicated factors. This mechanism study was public in an April 2023 preprint before the 2024 journal version. It does not establish a universal secretion mechanism, in-vivo benefit or a therapeutic result.
organization: University of California, San Francisco; Sharif University of Technology; McGill University

evidence.tested: Selected factors received perturbation and extracellular RNA-binding follow-up.
evidence.unknown: Generality across cell types and effects in vivo remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: ExoGRU gated recurrent neural network supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv API v1 metadata/abstract and journal PMC selected model, validation and limitations text; supplement not reviewed.
